Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 40, English)
Old Mantra, New Devta: Why the Newest Form of God Works Fastest, and Why the Oldest Name Still Matters Most

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn class continuing the institute's Kul Devta series, built ar ound an extended personal case study — Bhaiya's own kul devta, "Rameshwar Sarkar" (Rama Sarkar) — to explain why newer incarnations of the divine perform faster miracles, why the oldest mantras r emain the most powerful r egar dless, and why combining the two thr ough a guru pr oduces the fastest possible r esults.
1. Welcome and Standing Guidance for New Members

1. Bhaiya opens by welcoming first-time attendees, reminding them that no one arrives at Ashaeiynn by their own will alone — some subtle-body connection or karmic bond is what brought them, and he bows to them through that same connecting force. 2. Standing advice r epeated for newcomers: watch the institute's "Mool Tatva" (foundational teaching) video series, stay connected with one's assigned mentor , and make full use of the time spent at Ashaeiynn while one's own subtle body remains "awakened" enough to be here — since this teaching holds that a person's presence at Ashaeiynn lasts only as long as their subtle body remains in that receptive state.
2. The Cor e Premise: Lifespan Shrinks Across the Yugas, But Power Increases Dramatically

1. This teaching's central pr emise for the session: as we move fr om Satyug toward Kalyug, average lifespan decr eases sharply , but available spiritual energy/power increases dramatically . This is illustrated through an extended personal case study rather than abstract claims.
3. Case Study: Bhaiya's Own Kul Devta, "Rameshwar Sarkar" (Rama Sarkar)

1. Bhaiya intr oduces his own personal kul devta — explicitly framed as a claim about his own family lineage only , not a comparative ranking of anyone else's deity: a form of Bhagwan Ram (name also "Rama"), whose lineage Bhaiya's own family descends from. 2. This kul devta took birth in 1401 CE — for historical context, Bhaiya notes this predates the Qutub Minar's construction under Qutubuddin Aibak, and predates the Khilji dynasty and Prithviraj Chauhan/Mauryan-era references as well. 3. This incarnation is described as a Vishnu avatar , specifically in the form of Bhagwan Krishna, and lived only 30 years befor e voluntarily taking samadhi (a conscious departur e from the body) at that age.
4. Why This 30-Y ear Incarnation's Miracles Reportedly Exceeded Ram and Krishna's Combined

1. Bhaiya states that in just 30 years, this incarnation performed miracles r eportedly exceeding, combined, those attributed to Bhagwan Ram and Bhagwan Krishna's entir e lifetimes — with repeated instances of restoring the dead to life, both humans and animals, cited as one specific recurring example (including reviving a close friend on the spot after the friend's death).

2. By contrast, this teaching notes that Krishna's own life narrative describes r eviving only one person — Parikshit Ji Maharaj, who was in the womb at the time — and no clear account of Ram dir ectly r estoring anyone to life (Ram's touch turning Ahilya back into a woman is noted as a dif ferent kind of miracle, not literal resurrection).
5. Why Newer Incarnations Reportedly Show Faster , Mor e Frequent Miracles

1. This teaching's key claim: as Vishnu's avatars have pr ogr essed through the yugas, the number and speed of miracles attributed to each successive avatar has incr eased. By Kalyug, this teaching states miracles from newer forms have become almost routine rather than rare, extraordinary events. 2. An illustrative folk example given: a mother in Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, or Kolkata kneading dough while casually promising a small ₹10 of fering to a local "Peer Sahib" (a folk-shrine figure) if her child's minor ailment resolves — and the ailment resolving by the next day , described in this teaching as a routine, low-ef fort daily occurrence attributable to Bhagwan Ram/V ishnu's underlying shakti operating through that newer , localized form. 3. By contrast, this teaching claims the same r equest made formally and dir ectly to Bhagwan Krishna might take one to two months to r esolve, and the same r equest made dir ectly to Bhagwan Ram specifically could take years, or may not resolve thr ough that specific appr oach at all — attributed to Ram's own specific tattva now operating comparatively more slowly , since much of that underlying shakti has since taken further , newer forms.
6. The Appar ent Paradox: Newer Devtas Are Faster , But Older Mantras Are Mor e Powerful

1. This teaching intr oduces a key paradox: while newer incarnations/forms of the divine act faster and mor e frequently , the actual mantra (the sound/name itself) becomes MORE powerful the OLDER it is — meaning the oldest mantras (like the Ram naam / "tarak mantra") remain the single most potent mantras available, regardless of which specific, newer devta form a practitioner is ultimately trying to reach. 2. The practical r esolution offer ed: combining the oldest, most powerful mantra with the newest, fastest-acting devta form produces the str ongest possible combined r esult — living, visible miracles becoming achievable specifically through this combination.
7. Why the Newest Incarnation Carries the Most Accumulated Shakti

1. This teaching explains why newer incarnations carry mor e accumulated power: each successive Vishnu avatar (Narsimha in Satyug, then Ram in Treta, then Krishna in Dwapar , then further forms in Kalyug) gathers and r eabsorbs all the subtle bodies and accumulated devotional energy built up by devotees of every prior incarnation, once that prior incarnation's own body is r elinquished. This produces a continuously compounding pool of subtle-body ener gy carried forward into each newer form. 2. A supporting detail on invocation time acr oss yugas: Bhagwan Ram, arriving in Treta Yug, is described as already having been a fully self-aware/"awakened" divine being from birth, requiring no personal period of self-realization. Bhagwan Krishna, arriving in Dwapar Yug, is described as needing roughly two to four years of focused self-awakening before engaging fully with his divine role. By Kalyug, this teaching states the invocation/self-awakening period has gr own longer still — illustrated by Bhaiya's own kul devta needing a full 12 years of dedicated tapasya (repeating a single mantra) to fully awaken all the accumulated shakti carried forward from prior incarnations.
8. Why Kalyug's Incr eased "Impurity" Comes Packaged With Dramatically Incr eased Power

1. This teaching dir ectly addr esses a common complaint — that Kalyug is described as the age of maximum impurity (malinta) — by r eframing it: Kalyug also carries the maximum available spiritual power of any yuga. A person can become extremely impure in a single moment, but can also become extremely pure again just as quickly , given the power now available. 2. A specific comparative claim offer ed: purifying accumulated impurity that might have taken r oughly 400 years in Satyug, or 4 years in a later yuga, can now take mer e hours — or even mer e seconds — in Kalyug, pr ovided it's done

through consistent, single-pointed mantra jaap with genuine, unwavering faith. This teaching attributes this dramatic compression specifically to Kalyug's uniquely high available shakti, not to the mantra itself changing. 3. A further claim: wher eas past generations (illustratively , one's own grandpar ents or gr eat-grandpar ents) might have needed 10-15 years of sustained practice befor e receiving any siddhi at all, today's practitioners ar e described as having comparatively rapid access to genuine spiritual r esults — the limiting factor today , per this teaching, is not a shortage of available shakti but a shortage of practitioners' available time and sustained focus.
9. Why Everyone's Kul Devta Turns Out to Be the "Latest" Form, Never the Original Names

1. A specific pattern shar ed from r oughly a year of running weekly Kul Devta identification sessions at Ashaeiynn (covering, by Bhaiya's estimate, at least several thousand people so far): not a single person's identified kul devta has turned out to literally be named "Bhagwan Krishna" or "Bhagwan Ram" by name. 2. This teaching's explanation: every family's kul devta consistently turns out to be whichever mor e recent, "latest" incarnate form of that same underlying Vishnu or Shiv shakti is pr esiding over their specific lineage — described as an intentional, ongoing "suspense," where the specific newest form dif fers by family , but the underlying pattern (always latest, never the original named avatar) holds consistently .
10. Why a Practitioner Should Never Approach Their Kul Devta Dir ectly Without a Guru

1. A direct caution: attempting to appr oach or invoke one's kul devta dir ectly , without a guru as intermediary , risks interference from one's own pitru (ancestors) — since generations of prior family members will very likely have already worshipped that same kul devta long before the current practitioner arrived, creating an existing, tangled claim/relationship that a guru-mediated approach avoids. 2. This is offer ed as the cor e justification for why a guru (whether a living, spiritually awakened human guru, or a devta functioning in a guru r ole — Hanuman Ji Maharaj, in this teaching's own case) is described as essential — a devotee cannot properly "ask" their own kul devta for anything without this mediating relationship in place.
1 1. Bhaiya's Own Personal Practice: A Single Mantra, Routed Entir ely Through the Guru

1. Bhaiya states his own personal practice plainly: he gives no separate offering, invocation, or dedicated mantra dir ectly to his own kul devta — no separate ritual, no separate bhog, nothing invoked apart from what passes through his guru (Hanuman Ji Maharaj). 2. He notes this was not always the institute's practice — offerings to the kul devta's own mantra wer e previously made directly , until his guru explicitly instructed him to stop, and for roughly the past thr ee years, the exact same single mantra and single offering ("Jai Siya Ram") has been used for every form of worship at Ashaeiynn, r egardless of which deity (Rameshwar Sarkar , Ganesh Bhagwan, or any other) is being honor ed on a given occasion. 3. The stated personal formula: rather than dir ectly petitioning his kul devta, Bhaiya offers his practice entir ely to his guru, explicitly saying (in substance): "I only know the Jai Siya Ram mantra; I don't fully know my kul devta, though they appear befor e me; I am afraid to appr oach them dir ectly and don't consider myself capable — please pass this along to them if you judge it appr opriate, and if not, that's fine too; I bow to your feet regardless."
12. A Practical Accommodation for Newer Practitioners Still Building Trust in Their Guru

1. For members who haven't yet built full trust in this guru-r outed appr oach, Bhaiya offers a practical accommodation: dedicate r oughly 10-20% of one's daily personal jaap dir ectly toward one's own kul devta, while asking one's guru to ensure it reaches them — described as a reasonable bridge for those who want more direct reassurance while trust in the fully guru-routed method develops over time.
13. Why Sticking to a Single Mantra, Guru, and Devta Matters

1. This teaching's stated rationale for maintaining a single mantra, one guru, and one devta focus: switching between multiple mantras changes the specific "messenger" (mantradoot) associated with each mantra, which in turn changes the specific spiritual pathway/r oute being used — described as risking blocked "portal" access to the relevant realm (lok), communication barriers, and direct conflict between the accumulated ener gy of dif ferent mantras if practiced simultaneously . 2. The recommended practice: one mantra, one guru, one devta — consistently maintained — to avoid these specific complications and to allow a single mantra's power to compound steadily over time without interruption or dilution.
14. A Cautionary Personal Story: The "Surya Vigyan" Teaching That Once Shook People's Faith

1. Bhaiya shar es a cautionary personal account: r oughly a year prior , during a Mool Tatva class, he began r evealing a specific ar ea of teaching ("Surya Vigyan") that used a mathematical-paradox-style demonstration (illustratively , "proving" that 1 equals 2, or that 3 equals 4) to illustrate a deeper astral-world principle. 2. As soon as this specific teaching began, Bhaiya r eports dir ectly observing pr otective shakti visibly withdrawing fr om behind the listeners in real time — interpreted as a direct signal that this particular knowledge, however factually interesting or "practical," was destabilizing the listeners' underlying foundation of faith (much as "proving" that basic arithmetic can be internally inconsistent would undermine someone's trust in ordinary , functional mathematics, even though that same mathematics remains perfectly reliable and necessary for everyday use, like calculations in a phone or laptop). 3. Bhaiya r eports dir ectly asking his own guru afterward never to teach him anything that would cause people's faith/trust to waver this way again — while af firming that the deeper he personally trusts his guru, the more "practical," unusual knowledge his guru actually reveals to him privately , which Bhaiya has chosen not to pass on publicly again in this destabilizing form.
15. Closing Philosophy: Devotional Feeling (Bhaav) Must Never Be Sacrificed for Practical Knowledge

1. This teaching's closing principle: practical, analytical knowledge (gyaan) is valuable for solving pr oblems — one's own and, eventually , family members' — but devotional feeling (bhaav) must never be abandoned in the pr ocess of acquiring it, since bhaav is what actually keeps a person's guru-bond, and ther efor e their unseen protective support, intact. 2. A supporting principle: a practitioner's subconscious mind orientation matters dir ectly — the more emotionally devoted (bhaavuk) a person is, the more their subconscious mind is engaged on their behalf, and the more unseen subtle bodies and protective forces are described as working automatically for that person, beyond what conscious ef fort alone could achieve. Genuine devotees ar e described as characteristically emotional/devotional in natur e — which is also specifically why devotees ar e vulnerable to "hai" (the emotional harm/curse effect of someone's genuine grievance or ill will), precisely because of this heightened subconscious engagement. 3. Bhaiya's own stated r emedy whenever he notices himself becoming "too practical" or analytically detached: deliberately r eturn to r eading about the divine's character and conduct, seek the company of a genuine saint, or seek out someone capable of r estoring devotional feeling dir ectly — recommending the same practice to the sangat.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Lifespan decr eases acr oss the yugas fr om Satyug to Kalyug, but available spiritual power increases dramatically — illustrated through the case of Bhaiya's own kul devta ("Rameshwar Sarkar"/"Rama Sarkar"), born in 1401 CE, who reportedly performed more miracles in a 30-year lifetime than Ram and Krishna combined. Newer incarnations of the divine act faster and mor e frequently than older ones — a folk shrine's newer , localized form may resolve a request overnight, while the same request made to an older , more established form (like Bhagwan Ram directly) could take years or may not resolve that way at all. Despite this, the OLDEST mantras (like Ram naam / the tarak mantra) r emain the single most powerful mantras available , regardless of which specific newer devta form is ultimately being reached — combining the oldest mantra with the newest devta form produces the strongest possible combined result.

Each successive Vishnu avatar absorbs and carries forward the accumulated subtle-body energy of every prior incarnation's devotees — this is why later incarnations carry more compounded power , even as each yuga's specific selfawakening period (the time a new avatar needs to fully "wake up") grows longer . Kalyug's high impurity comes packaged with dramatically higher available power — purification that took centuries in earlier yugas can now take mere hours or seconds through consistent, faithful mantra jaap. Everyone's identified kul devta turns out to be the "latest" incarnate form of the underlying Vishnu/Shiv shakti presiding over their specific lineage — never the original named avatar (Ram or Krishna) dir ectly . Never appr oach your own kul devta dir ectly without a guru as intermediary — ancestors (pitru) who worshipped that same devta before you can create interference; a guru-mediated approach avoids this. Bhaiya's own personal practice channels everything thr ough a single mantra ("Jai Siya Ram") and his guru alone, with no separate offering made dir ectly to his own kul devta — newer practitioners still building guru-trust may instead dedicate roughly 10-20% of daily jaap directly to their own kul devta as a practical bridge. Stick to one mantra, one guru, and one devta consistently — switching between multiple mantras risks blocked spiritual "portal" access, communication barriers, and direct conflict between dif ferently-accumulated ener gies. Devotional feeling (bhaav) must never be sacrificed for purely practical/analytical spiritual knowledge — destabilizing "too clever" knowledge (illustrated by a cautionary "Surya Vigyan" teaching that once visibly weakened listeners' protective shakti) should be avoided; a devotee's emotional engagement is what keeps unseen protective forces actively working on their behalf. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 40, English)
Old Mantra, New Devta: Why the Newest Form of God Works Fastest, and Why the Oldest Name Still Matters Most
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Kul Devta live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

A: Per this teaching, a mother kneading dough might casually promise a small ₹10 of fering to a local "Peer Sahib" (a folk-shrine figure) if her child's minor ailment resolves — and the ailment resolves by the next day , described as a routine, low-ef fort daily occurrence. Q8. If newer devta forms act faster , does that mean older mantras like Ram naam ar e now less powerful? The oldest mantras (like Ram naam / the tarak mantra) remain the single most potent mantras available, regardless of which newer devta form a practitioner is ultimately trying to reach.

Q9. So what's the practical takeaway fr om this paradox? A: Per this teaching, combining the oldest, most powerful mantra with the newest, fastest-acting devta form produces the strongest possible combined result — living, visible miracles becoming achievable specifically through this combination.

Q10. Why do newer incarnations carry mor e accumulated power in the first place? A: This teaching explains that each successive Vishnu avatar (Narsimha in Satyug, then Ram in Treta, then Krishna in Dwapar , then further forms in Kalyug) gathers and reabsorbs all the subtle bodies and accumulated devotional ener gy built up by devotees of every prior incarnation, once that prior incarnation's own body is relinquished — producing a continuously compounding pool of ener gy .

Q1 1. Did every avatar take the same amount of time to "wake up" into their divine r ole? A: No — per this teaching, Bhagwan Ram (Treta Yug) was already fully self-aware/awakened from birth, needing no self-realization period. Bhagwan Krishna (Dwapar Yug) needed roughly two to four years. By Kalyug, this period has grown longer still — Bhaiya's own kul devta reportedly needed a full 12 years of dedicated tapasya (repeating a single mantra) to fully awaken the accumulated shakti carried forward from prior incarnations.

Q12. Kalyug is often described as the most impur e age — doesn't that make spiritual practice harder now? A: This teaching reframes that complaint: Kalyug also carries the maximum available spiritual power of any yuga. A person can become extremely impure in a single moment, but can also become extremely pure again just as quickly , given the power now available.

Q13. How much faster can purification actually happen in Kalyug, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, purifying accumulated impurity that might have taken roughly 400 years in Satyug, or 4 years in a later yuga, can now take mere hours — or even mere seconds — in Kalyug, provided it's done through consistent, single-pointed mantra jaap with genuine, unwavering faith. This is attributed to Kalyug's uniquely high available shakti, not to any change in the mantra itself.

Q14. Does that mean today's practitioners have it easier than their grandpar ents' generation? A: In terms of available shakti, yes — per this teaching, past generations might have needed 10-15 years of sustained practice before receiving any siddhi at all, while today's practitioners have comparatively rapid access to genuine spiritual results. The limiting factor today isn't a shortage of available shakti, but a shortage of practitioners' available time and sustained focus.

Q15. Has anyone at Ashaeiynn ever identified their kul devta as literally being named "Krishna" or "Ram"? A: No — per this teaching, across roughly a year of running weekly Kul Devta identification sessions covering, by Bhaiya's estimate, at least several thousand people, not a single person's identified kul devta has turned out to be literally named "Bhagwan Krishna" or "Bhagwan Ram."

Q16. Then why does this keep happening? A: This teaching's explanation: every family's kul devta consistently turns out to be whichever more recent, "latest" incarnate form of that same underlying Vishnu or Shiv shakti is presiding over their specific lineage — an intentional, ongoing "suspense," where the specific newest form dif fers by family , but the underlying pattern (always latest, never the original named avatar) holds consistently .

Q17. Can I just appr oach my own kul devta dir ectly if I want their blessing? A: This teaching cautions strongly against it — attempting to approach or invoke one's kul devta directly , without a guru as intermediary , risks interference from one's own pitru (ancestors), since generations of prior family members will very likely have already worshipped that same kul devta long before the current practitioner arrived, creating an existing, tangled claim/relationship.

A: Per this teaching, this is the core justification for why a guru (a living, spiritually awakened human guru, or a devta functioning in a guru role — Hanuman Ji Maharaj, in Bhaiya's own case) is essential — a devotee cannot properly "ask" their own kul devta for anything without this mediating relationship in place.

Q19. Does Bhaiya personally worship his own kul devta dir ectly? A: No — Bhaiya states plainly that he gives no separate of fering, invocation, or dedicated mantra directly to his own kul devta. No separate ritual, no separate bhog — nothing invoked apart from what passes through his guru, Hanuman Ji Maharaj.

Q20. Was this always Bhaiya's practice? A: No — per this teaching, of ferings to the kul devta's own mantra were previously made directly , until Bhaiya's guru explicitly instructed him to stop. For roughly the past three years, the exact same single mantra and single of fering ("Jai Siya Ram") has been used for every form of worship at Ashaeiynn, regardless of which deity is being honored on a given occasion.

Q21. What does Bhaiya actually say/offer to his guru r egarding his own kul devta? A: In substance: "I only know the Jai Siya Ram mantra; I don't fully know my kul devta, though they appear before me; I am afraid to approach them directly and don't consider myself capable — please pass this along to them if you judge it appropriate, and if not, that's fine too; I bow to your feet regardless."

Q22. I haven't built full trust in this guru-r outed appr oach yet — is ther e a middle gr ound? A: Yes — per this teaching, Bhaiya of fers a practical accommodation for members still building that trust: dedicate roughly 10-20% of one's daily personal jaap directly toward one's own kul devta, while asking one's guru to ensure it reaches them. This is a reasonable bridge while trust in the fully gururouted method develops over time.

Q25. What was the "Surya Vigyan" teaching that Bhaiya now avoids sharing? A: Per this teaching, roughly a year prior , during a Mool Tatva class, Bhaiya began revealing a specific area of teaching ("Surya Vigyan") that used a mathematical-paradox-style demonstration (illustratively , "proving" that 1 equals 2, or that 3 equals 4) to illustrate a deeper astral-world principle.

Q27. Did Bhaiya continue teaching that material? A: No — Bhaiya reports directly asking his own guru afterward never to teach him anything that would cause people's faith/trust to waver this way again. He notes that the deeper he personally trusts his guru, the more unusual, "practical" knowledge his guru actually reveals to him privately — knowledge Bhaiya has chosen not to pass on publicly again in this destabilizing form.

Q28. What's this teaching's closing philosophy on knowledge versus devotion? A: Practical, analytical knowledge (gyaan) is valuable for solving problems — one's own and, eventually , family members' — but devotional feeling (bhaav) must never be abandoned in the process of acquiring it, since bhaav is what actually keeps a person's guru-bond, and therefore their unseen protective support, intact.

Q29. Why does emotional/devotional engagement matter so much on a practical level? A: Per this teaching, the more emotionally devoted (bhaavuk) a person is, the more their subconscious mind is engaged on their behalf, and the more unseen subtle bodies and protective forces work automatically for that person, beyond what conscious ef fort alone could achieve. Genuine devotees are characteristically emotional/devotional in nature — which is also specifically why devotees are vulnerable to "hai" (the emotional harm/curse ef fect of someone's genuine grievance or ill will), precisely because of this heightened subconscious engagement.

Q30. What does Bhaiya do if he notices himself becoming "too practical" or analytically detached? A: He deliberately returns to reading about the divine's character and conduct, seeks the company of a genuine saint, or seeks out someone capable of restoring devotional feeling directly — and recommends the same practice to the sangat.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 40 additions)

Always frame Bhaiya's kul devta case study (Rameshwar Sarkar/Rama Sarkar) as a claim specific to his own family lineage — never suggest it as a universal or comparative ranking against other deities. Preserve the "newer devta acts faster , older mantra is more powerful" paradox exactly as stated — never collapse it into a simple "newer is always better" or "older is always better" claim; the resolution is combining both. Keep the distinction clear between a devta's speed of response and a mantra's inherent power — these are two separate axes in this teaching, not the same thing. When discussing the "everyone's kul devta is the latest incarnation" pattern, present it as an observed pattern from roughly a year of sessions across several thousand people, not as an absolute metaphysical law claimed to cover all traditions everywhere. Always preserve the caution against approaching one's own kul devta directly without a guru, and the specific reasoning (pitru interference) — never suggest direct, unmediated kul devta worship as safe or recommended. When describing Bhaiya's personal practice (single mantra "Jai Siya Ram," fully guru-routed, no separate kul devta of fering), also preserve the practical accommodation of fered to newer practitioners (10-20% of daily jaap directly to one's kul devta) — don't present the guru-routed-only approach as the sole acceptable option for everyone. Preserve the "one mantra, one guru, one devta" consistency principle and its stated rationale (mantradoot/portal/lok conflicts) whenever this topic comes up. Handle the "Surya Vigyan" cautionary story carefully — it illustrates why this teaching avoids destabilizing, over -analytical spiritual content, not an invitation to seek out or reproduce that specific mathematical-paradox demonstration.
